name: Vladimir Lenin
role: Bolshevik revolutionary and head of Soviet government (1917–1924)
summary: Lenin was the Bolshevik leader who led the October 1917 insurrection and headed the Soviet government until 1924, arguing for a vanguard party, the dictatorship of the proletariat and soviets in place of parliament. In power his government nationalised land, banks, foreign trade and large industry, separated church and state, liberalised marriage and divorce, dissolved the Constituent Assembly, outlawed opposition parties and used terror, before turning in 1921 to the New Economic Policy of controlled markets and concessions.

widespread-small-property.rationale: His 1917 programme warns the rural proletariat against the false attraction of petty farming, which can never abolish mass poverty, and calls for social ownership.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: Under the divorce decree he signed, a marriage is dissolved on the request of either spouse alone, the absent spouse being summoned only to settle names, custody and maintenance.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: He said full female emancipation required socialising the economy and participation in common productive labour.

women-must-cover.rationale: No recorded position found in the sources reviewed.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: The Decree on Land gives the right to use land to all citizens without distinction of sex.

women-suffrage.rationale: He insisted on women’s political equality and mass participation in governing the Soviet republic.

work-for-welfare.rationale: He explicitly defended the rule that those who do not work should not eat.

worker-farmer-alliance.rationale: He wrote that an honest coalition of workers and the working and exploited peasants is both possible and necessary, since their interests do not radically diverge.

worker-ownership.rationale: He advocated mass cooperative organisation as the route to socialist production under workers’ state power.

workers-anti-imperialist-capitalist-alli.rationale: His theses tell the Communist International to enter a temporary alliance with bourgeois democracy in colonial and backward countries, but never to merge with it.

workers-councils.rationale: His Declaration of Rights of the Working and Exploited People proclaimed a Republic of Soviets in which all power, centrally and locally, is vested in the soviets, and his government dissolved the Constituent Assembly in their favour.

workers-nation.rationale: He joined national self-determination to the international unity of proletarian struggle.

workers-own-party.rationale: He urged independent revolutionary working-class politics rather than subordination to bourgeois ideology.

workers-parties-campaign-reforms.rationale: He wrote that, unlike the anarchists, Marxists recognise the struggle for reforms that improve workers' conditions, while fighting reformism.

workplace-democracy.rationale: He defended independent factory management based on one-man responsibility, while preserving a consultative union role.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: He described imperialism as high monopoly profits for a handful of very rich countries drawn from the exploitation of other countries and colonies.

notes: Later pass (claude-opus-5-5, 2026-11-10) to rules 5: sources tagged as actions or words, Wikipedia no longer cited, candidate statements answered, and record over words applied to his time as Chairman of the Council of People's Commissars (1917-1924). His record is the decrees, draft decrees, orders and telegrams he wrote, moved or signed (Decree on Peace and on Land, the Declaration of Rights of the Working and Exploited People, the press decree, the Kadet decree, the dissolution of the Constituent Assembly, the decrees on conscience, marriage, divorce, estates, foreign trade, nationalisation and monuments, the Penza telegram, the 1921 Georgia telegrams and his 1922 drafts for the Criminal Code); these now answer statements earlier answered from his words (democracy, opposition, press, religion, divorce, recall, salaries, secession). Self-determination is answered as mixed: his government recognised Finland but he authorised the occupation of Georgia in 1921. Several 0 answers left at high confidence were lowered to low, as mixed evidence. Themes searched in his collected works (Marxists Internet Archive, local corpus) and the First Decrees of Soviet Power: taxation, money and banking, land and housing, trade, labour and welfare, education, family and abortion, religion and atheism, language and nationality, colonies and the Comintern, war, disarmament and insurrection, courts and terror, elections and recall, party discipline. Not covered by his writings or record: LGBT questions, drugs, gun ownership, environment and ecology, technology beyond electrification, immigration and most modern policy questions, which stay null.
